title: Read Daniel's hand edit to Tomato
tier_reason: reading his edit and writing down what it implies — nothing to walk back
ask: Daniel hand-edited Tomato in the sprite editor and said he was fixing: "Removing white tiles that should be transparent". The measurement: Tomato: 17 pixels across 4 frames (frame 1, frame 2, frame 3, frame 4). Colors dropped: #f8f4e6. The silhouette moved, not just the interior shading. Look at it against the style guide draft and the rest of the sheet, and say in a few lines what his edit is telling you about the direction — whether it agrees with the guide, quietly contradicts it, or repeats something he has done before. If it is just tidying and there is nothing to learn, say exactly that in one line; a short honest answer beats manufactured significance. Do not propose amendments to the guide yet; he wants a look session before it is signed. This is evidence-gathering for that session.
first_action: Open assets/sprites/generated/tomato.png and the ledger entry (step 1) in HQ, compare it with the style guide in docs/design/09-art-direction.md, and write down what the edit says about his taste.

result:
Read the tomato ledger against the sheet and the guide.

**It is the sixth time, not the first.** Characters (twice), animals, obstacles (twice), now tomato — same colour every time, `#f8f4e6`, the image pipeline's cream backdrop, left opaque in negative space the keying step can't reach because the sprite encloses it on all four sides. Six sittings, and his note is nearly word-for-word the one he wrote on 3 September. The fix for it and the sweep of the sheets already in the build were both written up on 7 September and neither has landed. Tomato is the receipt for that.

**One thing in it is genuinely new, and it matters.** He recoloured this time. Frame 3 got two recoloured pixels, frame 4 got one, and no new colour entered the sheet. Every previous keying edit of his was one hundred percent erasure — punch the plate out, leave what's left. Here he erased the backdrop and then closed the edge behind it, using colours already on the sheet. So the standard has moved a step: it isn't just *the backdrop is not part of the object*, it's *the outline that's exposed when the backdrop goes has to be a finished edge, not a hole*. That's the first time his hand has said anything about how a silhouette is drawn rather than where it stops, and it's worth carrying into the look session.

**It also lands on a crop, which none of the others did.** The ripe cue we ruled yesterday rides on these four cells. The glow colour is safe — tomato's `#c84e39` was hand-sampled off the fruit body, not averaged, so backdrop never got into it. The silhouette numbers the crop pages print were counting cream as plant, but those are computed off the sheet each time, so they corrected themselves the moment he saved.

**Against the guide: still no contradiction, and still the same silence.** Every rule in the draft is about colour — ramps, coloured outlines, saturation-pop, reserved hues. Six sittings and he has not touched one of them by hand. His entire recorded taste is about the boundary of the sprite and now the quality of that boundary. That's the finding I want to open the look session with.

**What this implies.** Nothing here is a taste call — it's a defect he has been performing by hand six times while the fix sits filed. Accepting this starts the pipeline fix, the sweep of the sheets in the build, and one line in my session notes.
